prompt: Implement snapshot_views(initial, events), a deterministic committed-version/private-overlay visibility model for ordinary Read Committed ('rc') and Repeatable Read ('rr') observations. It is not a SQL parser, lock manager, conflict validator or full PostgreSQL executor. initial is a native dict of 0–8 key IDs to native integer values in [-1000,1000]. events is a native list of 0–64 exact records. All IDs match case-sensitive ASCII [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,11}; transaction and key namespaces are separate. At most 8 distinct transaction IDs and 8 distinct key IDs occur across the call, including initial keys. Event schemas: {op:'begin',tx,isolation:'rc'|'rr'}; {op:'read',tx,key}; {op:'scan',tx,minimum:int}; {op:'write',tx,key,value:int_or_None}; {op:'commit',tx}; {op:'abort',tx}; {op:'external_commit',changes:{key:int_or_None}}. minimum and every integer value are in [-1000,1000], excluding bool. None in a write/change means deletion/absence, never a stored SQL NULL. Each begin uses a previously unused transaction ID; all other tx events name a currently active transaction. External changes can contain 0–8 keys. Pending transactions at the end are allowed and are not implicitly committed. The caller supplies successful/admissible private table changes: no two active transactions privately write the same key, no competing commit modifies a key privately held by an active writer, and a Repeatable Read write does not target a key changed after its captured snapshot; actual lock waits, write failures, triggers and constraint validation are outside this analyzer. No invalid-input validation is required. Start with abstract commit epoch 0 containing initial. Every commit/external_commit increments epoch by one, including an empty commit, and atomically publishes its changes as versions at that epoch; this counter is neither a PostgreSQL transaction ID nor a WAL LSN. Abort publishes nothing and does not increment epoch. Begin captures NO snapshot. An rr transaction captures the current committed epoch when its first read, scan OR write event occurs and retains it thereafter. Each rc read/scan uses the current committed epoch for that command. Every observation first takes the newest committed version of each key at or before its selected epoch, then applies that transaction's own successful private writes/deletions regardless of whether they are newer than that external snapshot. Other transactions' private writes are never visible. Write acquires an rr snapshot if needed, then changes only that transaction's private overlay; commit publishes the entire overlay and ends the transaction, while abort discards it. Read returns the selected key's integer value, or None for absence. Scan returns all visible nondeleted keys whose values are >=minimum, sorted by ordinary ASCII/Python key order. Return exactly {epoch:int,committed:{key:int},observations:[records]}. epoch is the final commit epoch; committed is the final latest committed nondeleted key map, ignoring all pending overlays. Append one observation only for each read/scan in event order. Read records are exactly {op:'read',tx,epoch,key,value}; scan records are exactly {op:'scan',tx,epoch,rows:[{key,value}]}. The observation epoch is the selected external snapshot even when own overlay changes its returned rows. Empty inputs return epoch0, a fresh initial-state copy and observations[]. All containers/scalars are exact native dict/list/str/int/None types; bool does not replace int. Every mutable output container must be fresh, pairwise independent and disjoint from all inputs and earlier results. Inputs and prior output values/native types remain unchanged through later calls. Use only standard-library computation/allocation, with no actual database/runtime invocation, raw memory, threads or network.

Implement precedence_graph(transactions, operations=None). This is a finite completed SINGLE-VERSION read/write history whose modeled transactions all commit. It classifies conflict serializability, not current lock waits, recoverability, arbitrary read-from validity, broader view equivalence or equal final values. transactions is a native list of 0..8 distinct case-sensitive ASCII IDs matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}, in any input order. Named transactions with no operations remain vertices. operations is None (default, interpreted as empty) or a native list of 0..64 exact dicts {tx,kind,key}. tx names a listed transaction; kind is native str 'read' or 'write'; key is an opaque case-sensitive ASCII ID with the same grammar, in a separate namespace. At most 16 distinct keys occur. The list gives atomic operation order. Empty transactions requires empty/None operations. Add edge A->B for EVERY ordered pair of positions i<j with different transactions, the SAME key, and at least one write. Include nonadjacent pairs. Read/read and same-transaction pairs create no edge. Deduplicate edges. Return exactly {edges,acyclic,order} as a native dict. edges is a native list of fresh two-string lists [source,target], lexicographically sorted by (source,target). acyclic is native bool. order is None if any directed cycle exists; otherwise it is a native list containing the lexicographically smallest topological order over ALL named vertices. Produce that order by repeatedly choosing the smallest currently zero-indegree vertex, not sorting an arbitrary completed order afterward. Empty graph returns edges=[],acyclic=True,order=[]; an edgeless named graph returns sorted transaction IDs. ID comparisons use ASCII/Python str ordering without locale or case folding. All containers/scalars have exact stated built-in dict/list/str/bool/None types. Inputs satisfy the complete domain; no invalid-input behavior is required. Every returned mutable container must be distinct from every input container, every other returned container and all earlier results. Inputs and their native types must remain unchanged during this and later calls. Earlier returned values and native types must remain unchanged through later calls. Use only standard-library ordinary computation/allocation; no actual database/runtime, network, threads, raw memory or external execution. The checker runs the candidate in a subprocess with a five-second timeout.

Implement wal_trace(records, events, initial_pages=None), a bounded deterministic physical WAL-prefix model, not a database, visibility engine or hardware test. Logical record positions are one-based LSNs, not byte offsets. records is a native list of 0–32 exact dicts: {kind:'page',page:ID,value:int} or {kind:'commit',tx:ID}. At most 16 page IDs and 16 transaction IDs occur; each transaction ID has exactly one commit marker. Page and transaction ID namespaces are separate and may use the same spelling. IDs match ASCII [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. Values are native ints from -1000 through 1000, excluding bool. All records are complete and already generated in volatile memory. Page records are physical redo images; they do not model transaction-visible rows, aborts or undo. initial_pages is None, meaning zero-valued base pages for all logged page IDs, or a native dict ID→value covering every logged page, with at most 16 entries total. Extra unchanged base pages are allowed. All base pages have LSN 0.

events is a native list of 0–64 exact dicts processed serially. Initially volatile-written frontier W=0 and durable frontier D=0. {op:'write',through:int} advances the entire contiguous volatile-written prefix, with oldW<=through<=len(records). {op:'flush',through:int} advances the durable prefix, with oldD<=through<=W. {op:'page_write',lsn:int} refers to a page record at 1<=lsn<=len(records), and its lsn is not below that page's currently persisted LSN. Admit the supplied image and copy its value/LSN only if D>=lsn; otherwise pages remain unchanged. {op:'ack',tx:ID,mode:'sync'|'async'} refers to a known commit marker. Async records an acknowledgment immediately. Sync ALWAYS tests whether D covers that marker, even if an earlier async acknowledgment is already recorded; if not, report awaiting-flush without removing the historical acknowledgment. Successful repeated acknowledgments deduplicate the set.

At most one {op:'crash',redo_start:int} occurs, only as the last event. It deterministically loses every log position>D and sets W=D; positions<=D survive. redo_start is in 1..D+1 and describes a valid checkpoint: every page record before redo_start and within the durable prefix is already covered by that page's persisted LSN. Recovery scans every record position from redo_start through D, including commit markers. Apply a page record only when its LSN exceeds that page's currently persisted LSN, and record which positions were applied. No additional crash or I/O error occurs. Deterministically losing the whole volatile tail is a model choice, not a claim that all real unflushed bytes necessarily disappear.

Return a native list containing an INITIAL snapshot followed by one snapshot per event. Each snapshot has exactly {written:int,durable:int,pages:{ID:{lsn:int,value:int}},acknowledged:[sorted tx IDs],durable_commits:[sorted tx IDs],event_result:None|str,recovery:None|dict}. Durable commits are all commit markers at positions<=D, even if never acknowledged. Initially acknowledgments are empty and event_result/recovery are None. Event result strings: write→'written'; flush→'flushed'; admitted page_write→'page-written'; blocked page_write→'wal-blocked'; successful/repeated acknowledgment→'acknowledged'; blocked sync acknowledgment→'awaiting-flush'; crash→'recovered'. Only the crash snapshot has non-None recovery, exactly {scanned:[ordered LSNs],applied:[ordered applied page LSNs],lost_acknowledged:[sorted historically acknowledged tx IDs absent from durable_commits]}. The historical acknowledged set remains recorded after crash.

Inputs satisfy all static and dynamic preconditions; no outside-domain validation is required. Every integer domain excludes bool. All types are the stated exact built-in list/dict/str/int/None types. Preserve all input values/types and every prior result through later calls. Every returned mutable container must be distinct within and across snapshots/calls and from all inputs. Defaults, empty calls and repeated calls are part of the interface. Use only the Python standard library and ordinary computation/allocation, with no real database, storage, raw memory, threads, network or external runtime invocation.

Implement index_access(required_columns, index_columns, candidates, supports_index_only=True), a deterministic PostgreSQL-style candidate-visibility model, not a real query planner or database. required_columns and index_columns are native lists of 0–8 distinct ASCII identifiers matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. supports_index_only is an exact bool. candidates is a native list of 0–32 exact dicts {id:ID,index_values:{column:int},heap_values:{column:int},vm_all_visible:bool,heap_visible:bool}, with distinct candidate IDs of the same identifier grammar. index_values has exactly index_columns as keys; heap_values has exactly the union of required_columns and index_columns. Shared index/heap values agree for the same tuple. Payloads are native ints -1000..1000, excluding bool. All candidates already satisfy the index-search predicate; no additional residual filtering is modeled. heap_visible is the supplied correct visibility result for the selected read snapshot. A valid true vm_all_visible implies heap_visible=True; false VM does not determine visibility. These conditions remain stable during the call; invalid combinations are outside the domain.

Select strategy 'index-only' iff supports_index_only is true and every required column occurs in index_columns; otherwise select 'heap'. This declared eligibility policy is not a claim that PostgreSQL always selects an eligible index-only plan over other costed plans. In index-only strategy, a true VM bit avoids heap checking and admits the candidate. A false VM bit requires exactly one candidate heap visibility check and admits it only if heap_visible is true. An admitted index-only candidate still projects from index_values after a required heap visibility check. In heap strategy, check every candidate's heap visibility regardless of VM, and project admitted values from heap_values. Invisible candidates produce no row. An empty required_columns list is a permitted modeled projection yielding empty values dicts, not a promise about concrete SQL projection syntax.

Return exactly {strategy:str,heap_checks:int,rows:[{id:ID,values:{required_column:int}}],trace:[{id:ID,heap_checked:bool,visible:bool,value_source:'index'|'heap'|None}]}. Preserve candidate order in rows, omitting invisible candidates, and in trace, with one entry per candidate. heap_checks counts candidate checking operations, not physical disk reads. value_source is None for invisible candidates and otherwise identifies the selected projection source. Empty candidates returns empty rows/trace and zero checks, with strategy still determined by columns and support.

Inputs satisfy the complete bounded domain, so no invalid-input validation is required. All types are the stated exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None types. Preserve every input and all prior output values/types through later calls. Every returned mutable container must be distinct within its result, across calls and from all inputs. Defaults, empty calls and repeated calls are included. Use only the standard library and ordinary computation/allocation, with no real database, profiler, hardware, raw memory, threads, network or external runtime/compiler invocation.

Implement compact_key(records, last_sequence, snapshots=None, deeper_overlap=False). This bounded model applies LevelDB 1.23 SAME-USER-KEY record omission rules for a successfully installed nontrivial compaction output/current Version. It does not erase all physical input copies or model file selection, other keys, concurrent mutation, I/O errors or file cleanup. Engine ordering and selection invariants are supplied preconditions. records is a native list of 0..64 exact dicts {sequence,kind,value}, strictly descending by distinct sequence. last_sequence is a native int in 0..1000000. Each sequence is a native int in 1..last_sequence. kind is native str 'value' or 'delete'. A value record has a native str value of 0..32 printable ASCII characters (codepoints 32..126), including empty string. A delete record has value=None. All records represent one implicit key. snapshots is None (default) or a native list of 0..16 native ints in 0..last_sequence; duplicate snapshot sequences are allowed. If snapshots is nonempty, horizon=min(snapshots); otherwise horizon=last_sequence. This is the oldest retained explicit snapshot at the modeled compaction decision. deeper_overlap is a native bool, default False, saying whether ANY file RANGE at levels L+2 or deeper covers this key for an L-to-L+1 compaction. True does not assert an actual key entry exists there; False is the supplied safe base-level fact. Process records newest to oldest, remembering the preceding INPUT sequence even when that preceding record was dropped. FIRST, if a preceding sequence exists and preceding<=horizon, drop the current record with reason 'shadowed', regardless of its kind or deeper_overlap. OTHERWISE, if current kind='delete', current sequence<=horizon and deeper_overlap=False, drop it with reason 'obsolete_deletion'. OTHERWISE keep it. Update preceding to the current sequence after EVERY decision. Return exactly {horizon,kept,dropped} as a native dict. horizon is a native int. kept is a native list of fresh full record copies in original descending order. dropped is a native list of fresh exact dicts {sequence,reason}, also in input order; reasons are exactly the two strings above. If both tests could justify dropping, the FIRST rule determines reason. Empty records is valid, including last_sequence=0, and produces both output lists empty. A shadowed tombstone is not protected merely by deeper_overlap=True; an otherwise-unshadowed tombstone is not discarded merely because it predates the horizon. All integers exclude bool; every container/scalar has its exact stated built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None type. Inputs satisfy the complete domain, so no outside-domain validation is required. Every returned mutable container must be distinct from every input, every other returned container and earlier results. Inputs and their native types remain unchanged during this and later calls; earlier output values and native types also remain unchanged through later calls. Use only standard-library ordinary computation/allocation; no actual database, raw memory, threads, network or external runtime. The checker runs the candidate in a subprocess with a five-second timeout.
